title: Phosphorus-31 Bioenergetics
summary: 31P is spin 1/2 at 100 percent natural abundance with a gyromagnetic ratio of 17.235 MHz/T, so a 3T system runs at 51.7 MHz and a 7T at 120.6 MHz, with roughly 6.6 percent of the 1H sensitivity per nucleus. One acquisition gives PCr, the three ATP resonances, Pi, the phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters of membrane turnover, NAD and UDPG, plus intracellular pH from the Pi shift and free cytosolic Mg2+ from the ATP shifts. Sensitivity sets the working point: voxels of 10 to 100 mL, T1 values from 0.7 s for beta-ATP to about 7 s for PCr and Pi, and gamma-ATP T2 under 30 ms at 7T. Magnetization transfer across the PCr to ATP to Pi network is the only routine way to get a rate rather than a concentration.

facts.label: Nucleus properties
facts.value: Spin 1/2, 100 percent natural abundance, 17.235 MHz/T; 51.7 MHz at 3T, 120.6 MHz at 7T, about 6.6 percent of 1H sensitivity
facts.note: Metabolites sit at 1 to 35 mM against roughly 80 M 1H in tissue water, so the practical deficit is about four orders of magnitude and drives the large voxels.

facts.label: Chemical shift ladder, PCr at 0 ppm
facts.value: PE +6.8, PC +6.2, Pi +4.9 at pH 7.0, GPE +3.5, GPC +2.9, PCr 0.0, gamma-ATP -2.5, alpha-ATP -7.5, NAD(H) -8.3, UDPG -9.8 and -11.6, beta-ATP -16.2 ppm
facts.note: PE to beta-ATP spans about 23 ppm, which is 1.2 kHz at 3T and 2.8 kHz at 7T; the wider 31P scale for phosphorus chemistry runs to several hundred ppm but nothing in vivo lives out there.

facts.label: Resting skeletal muscle concentrations
facts.value: PCr 33 +/- 2 mM, ATP 8.2 +/- 0.4 mM, Pi 4.5 +/- 0.2 mM in human calf, per liter of cell water
facts.note: These are means across roughly ten calibrated 31P MRS studies; they are the denominators for every PCr depletion and recovery-rate calculation, so an error here propagates straight into mitochondrial capacity.

facts.label: Resting brain concentrations
facts.value: PCr and ATP both near 3 to 4 mM, Pi 1.0 to 1.3 mM, PE plus PC 1.72 +/- 0.29 mM, total NAD 0.3 to 0.4 mM
facts.note: ATP at 3 mM is commonly assumed as the internal concentration reference, which makes every other brain concentration conditional on that assumption.

facts.label: Intracellular pH from the Pi to PCr shift
facts.value: pH = 6.75 + log10((d - 3.27)/(5.63 - d)), d in ppm; resting values 7.02 to 7.05 in muscle and about 7.00 to 7.05 in brain
facts.note: Published constants range over pKa 6.75 to 6.77 and an alkaline limit of 5.63 to 5.69 ppm, worth up to 0.05 pH units of absolute offset, so state which form you used; sensitivity is about 0.01 pH per 0.01 ppm, and 0.01 ppm is 0.5 Hz at 3T.

facts.label: Free cytosolic Mg2+ from the ATP shifts
facts.value: About 0.18 mM in human occipital lobe; resting skeletal muscle is roughly twice that, with published values spanning about 0.3 to 1.0 mM
facts.note: The beta-ATP to PCr separation moves by roughly 3 ppm between Mg-free ATP near -19 ppm and fully complexed MgATP near -16 ppm; the spread in reported values is calibration curve, not physiology, since the curve must handle pH, ionic strength and competing ligands.

facts.label: T1 in human calf muscle, 3T versus 7T
facts.value: 3T: PCr 6.7 s, Pi 6.9 s, gamma-NTP 5.5 s, beta-NTP 3.9 s, alpha-NTP 3.4 s. 7T: PCr 4.0 s, Pi 6.3 s, gamma-NTP 3.3 s, alpha and beta-NTP 1.8 s
facts.note: 31P T1 values fall by up to 62 percent from 3T to 7T as chemical shift anisotropy takes over; on the figures above PCr itself falls 40 percent and beta-NTP 54 percent, so saturation corrections do not transfer between field strengths.

facts.label: The saturation problem
facts.value: At TR = T1 with a 90 degree pulse the signal recovers to about 63 percent of full, so roughly 37 percent is lost to saturation; full recovery of PCr at 3T needs TR near 33 s, while typical TR is 2 to 5 s
facts.note: PCr has the longest T1 and ATP the shortest, so an uncorrected PCr/ATP at short TR reads low; at TR 2 s and T1 4 s the Ernst angle is 53 degrees.

facts.label: T2 and T2*
facts.value: Calf muscle T2 at 3T: PCr 354 ms, Pi 153 ms, gamma-NTP 62 ms; at 7T: PCr 217 ms, Pi 109 ms, gamma-NTP 29 ms. Brain at 7T: PE 202 ms, PC 129 ms, GPE 214 ms, GPC 213 ms, Pi 86 ms. PCr linewidth in brain at 7T about 11.5 Hz, so T2* near 28 ms
facts.note: The 29 ms gamma-NTP T2 at 7T is what kills long-TE 31P spin echoes on the ATP peaks; Pi has a short T2 partly from fast reversible exchange with gamma-ATP, not from field inhomogeneity.

facts.label: PME and PDE
facts.value: PME spans about +5.5 to +7.5 ppm and is mostly PE and PC; PDE spans about +2 to +4 ppm and is mostly GPE and GPC, roughly 1 to 3 mM in brain
facts.note: PME are phospholipid precursors and PDE are breakdown products, but a broad, very short T2 component from mobile membrane phospholipid sits under the PDE region and has to be modelled or filtered or it inflates PDE.

facts.label: NAD and UDPG
facts.value: Total NAD 0.3 to 0.4 mM in human brain at 7T; reported NAD+/NADH between about 3 and 10. NAD+ appears as an AB quartet and NADH as a singlet near -8.3 ppm, with UDPG components near -9.8 and -11.6 ppm
facts.note: NAD(H) lies on the alpha-ATP foot, so the redox number depends entirely on how alpha-ATP and the UDP-sugar components are removed or modelled; the spread in published ratios is a methods disagreement, not biological variance.

facts.label: CK and ATPase flux by magnetization transfer
facts.value: Human brain at 7T: k(PCr to gamma-ATP) 0.38 +/- 0.02 per s and k(Pi to gamma-ATP) 0.19 +/- 0.02 per s; with brain PCr near 3.5 mM and Pi near 1.0 mM these give a forward CK flux near 1.3 mM/s and an ATP synthase flux near 0.2 mM/s
facts.note: The CK exchange flux is several times the net ATP turnover, so it measures exchange, not net synthesis; band inversion transfer or four-angle saturation transfer get these in a fraction of the time that classic saturation transfer plus a separate T1 measurement needs.

facts.label: Cardiac PCr/ATP
facts.value: Healthy myocardium 1.85 to 2.14 at 7T after blood correction, statistically indistinguishable from 3T but with roughly 2.7 times smaller Cramer-Rao uncertainty; heart T1 at 7T is PCr 3.05 +/- 0.41 s and gamma-ATP 1.82 +/- 0.09 s
facts.note: A ratio below about 1.6 has been associated with poor survival in dilated cardiomyopathy, which is why the blood and saturation corrections are not optional in cardiac work.

facts.label: 1H decoupling and NOE
facts.value: Decoupling at 3T narrows PE and PC by about 8 Hz, GPE and GPC by about 12 Hz, alpha-ATP by about 5 Hz; NOE gives about 30 +/- 9 percent PCr enhancement in brain at 7T, at a reported head-average SAR of 2.18 W/kg against the IEC head limit of 3.2 W/kg
facts.note: Decoupling buys the PME and PDE separation; NOE mostly buys SNR on PCr, and at 7T the SAR cost of NOE is poorly repaid, so many groups decouple and skip the NOE.

practice: Reference the spectrum to PCr at 0 ppm rather than an external standard. PCr is insensitive to pH and Mg2+ across the physiological range while Pi and the ATP peaks are exactly the things you are trying to read, and an external capillary sits in a different susceptibility environment.

Use adiabatic excitation, an adiabatic half passage or BIR-4, with a transmit-receive surface loop. B1 from a loop of radius a falls off steeply past one radius, so keep the region of interest within about one coil radius of the plane of the loop and let the adiabatic pulse flatten the flip angle over that depth.

Check that beta-ATP at -16.2 ppm still gets a usable flip angle. A hard pulse calibrated on PCr at 7T covers 2.8 kHz of offset badly and can cost tens of percent on beta-ATP, which is the peak carrying both the ATP concentration and the free Mg2+ reading.
Shim on the 1H water signal, then switch to 31P. A PCr linewidth much above 12 to 15 Hz in brain at 7T points at the shim or at motion, not at the 31P coil.

Measure T1 in your own voxel and cohort, or use a published TR and flip-angle pair matched to your field and tissue, and report the saturation factors you applied. Do not import 3T saturation corrections into a 7T study.

For exercise studies, run unlocalized or minimally localized pulse-acquire at TR of about 2 s with a modest flip angle and take the time resolution. PCr depletion, the Pi to PCr shift and the PCr recovery time constant are all ratios or shifts and tolerate partial saturation better than absolute concentrations do.

Fix coil and limb position before, during and after exercise. Any change in coil loading changes tuning, matching and the effective flip angle, and the PCr recovery kinetics you are fitting assume none of those moved.

For MT, prefer band inversion transfer or a four-angle saturation transfer scheme. Classic single-site saturation transfer needs a separate intrinsic T1 measurement and spills saturation onto neighbouring peaks at the linewidths you get in vivo.
pitfalls: Differential saturation biases PCr/ATP low at short TR because PCr has the longest T1 and ATP the shortest. Comparing an uncorrected ratio between two field strengths compares two different saturation states, not two tissues.

Blood 2,3-DPG resonates near +5.2 and +6.3 ppm, right on Pi and the low-field edge of the PME region. In heart, liver, tumour and any blood-rich voxel an apparently elevated Pi can simply be blood; the cardiac convention is to subtract about 15 percent of the total 2,3-DPG signal from gamma-ATP and to distrust Pi entirely.

Pi in resting muscle is not one pool. An alkaline, short-T1 Pi component has been detected in vivo, so fitting a single Lorentzian to Pi skews both the concentration and the pH, and during exercise fibre-type recruitment splits Pi into distinct pH pools that a one-peak fit averages away.

alpha-ATP overlaps NAD+, NADH and the UDP-sugars. Quoting alpha-ATP as an ATP measure overstates ATP, and quoting NAD+/NADH without a frequency-selective alpha-ATP inversion or an explicit UDPG model is a lineshape artefact rather than a redox measurement.

Proton decoupling at 7T is SAR limited, not hardware limited. A decoupling train through a large 1H coil can put head-average SAR near 2 W/kg on its own against a 3.2 W/kg head limit, which then forbids the short TR you wanted for averaging; budget SAR and TR together, not separately.

The pH you get is the signal-weighted average over every compartment contributing Pi in the voxel, including any extracellular or vascular Pi. A single number at 0.02 pH precision can still be wrong by more than that if the compartments are not what you assumed.
